title: Conditional independence and graphical models for rankings
claim: Mutual-exclusivity constraints on rankings can be relaxed by mapping them to coarser variables defined over a graph, grouping rankings into shared events.
layout: 2 panels, graph left and table right, color-coded rows
description: The figure has two parts. On the left is a small directed graph with three circled nodes. Node 1 sits at the top and has an arrow to node 2 at the lower left. Node 2 has an arrow to node 3 at the lower right. On the right is a table with columns σ, σ̄ and x, and a vertical rule before x. It has six rows, one for each permutation of three items, such as 1,2,3 and 3,2,1. The rows are shaded green, orange, blue, pink, yellow and purple. In the x column, rows that map to the same realization share a color. For example, the orange rows both give 1,2,1 and the blue rows both give 1,1,2. abstract: Ranking models define probability distributions over rankings and are fundamental in applications such as preference learning and decision-making. Without structural assumptions, these models are intractable due to their factorial complexity. Although independence assumptions are key to reducing complexity and enabling interpretability, standard notions of conditional independence must account for the mutual exclusivity constraints inherent to rankings. We introduce relative rank models, a probabilistic framework based on structured coarsenings of the ranking space that relax these constraints while preserving relative order information. This representation enables a well-defined notion of conditional independence for rankings and allows rankings to be modeled using Bayesian networks. As a result, standard methods for learning and probabilistic inference can be applied to rankings, with interpretable representations based on conditional independence. We further show that two prominent ranking models based on independence assumptions tailored to rankings arise as special cases, providing a unifying framework for independence in ranking models.
